verdict: Centene's revenue rose 2% to $50.6B, but medical costs ate 92.7% of premiums and premium taxes tipped the quarter to a small $65M loss — even though its underlying (adjusted) profit was $0.58 a share and it raised full-year guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $50.6B in total revenue, vs $49.7B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs adjusted EPS of $0.58 — see one-off items

kpis.label: Health benefits ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums spent on medical care — better than the company expected

kpis.label: Members
kpis.note: Down from 28.0M a year ago as Marketplace and Medicaid rolls shrank

segments.name: Medicaid
segments.note: Health coverage for low-income members paid by states — Centene's biggest line, helped by rate rises and state directed payments.

segments.name: Medicare
segments.note: Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement and the fast-growing Medicare prescription-drug plan (PDP), which reached 8.9M members.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Marketplace (Obamacare exchange) plans and other commercial coverage — revenue fell as Marketplace membership dropped to 3.4M from 5.8M.

segments.name: Premium tax
segments.note: Taxes states levy on premiums, billed to states as revenue and paid straight back as an expense below — it inflates both sides equally.

segments.name: Other premium & service
segments.note: Service fees and other smaller premium lines.

opex.name: Premium tax expense
opex.note: The premium taxes collected above, paid back to states — slightly more than was billed this quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — 7.2% of premium and service revenue (6.5% on the company's adjusted basis).

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Depreciation ($138M) plus amortization of acquired intangible assets ($161M) — a non-cash charge spreading past deal and asset costs over time.

takeaways.title: Medical costs beat the plan
takeaways.text: The health benefits ratio — medical costs as a share of premiums — was 92.7%, better than expected, driven by Medicare, with Medicaid and Marketplace on track. Centene raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.40 to more than $5.20 and cut its full-year HBR outlook to about 90.75%.

takeaways.title: Fewer members, more premium each
takeaways.text: Total membership fell to 25.7M from 28.0M a year ago — Marketplace dropped to 3.4M from 5.8M and Medicaid to 11.9M from 12.7M — but premium and service revenue still rose 0.5% to $45.1B on rate increases and growth in the Medicare drug plan, which added about a million members.

takeaways.title: Debt is coming down
takeaways.text: Centene cut debt by $1.1B during the quarter, including fully redeeming its 2027 senior notes in October. Operating cash flow was negative $3.7B in the quarter, a timing effect of premium and claims payment cycles.

oneTimers: GAAP results include $307M of pre-tax 'other adjustments' the company strips out of adjusted EPS — mainly $276M of severance from enterprise optimization and contract exits and $35M of related vendor costs, partly offset by an $18M net gain on real estate. With $161M of amortization of acquired intangibles also excluded, adjusted net earnings were $290M ($0.58 a share) versus a GAAP loss.
otherDetail: Other income of $185M, net: $333M of investment and other income plus a $1M gain on debt extinguishment, less $149M of interest expense.
footerNote: For a health insurer, medical costs and the cost of services play the role of cost of revenue. Net loss of $65M includes $6M of earnings attributable to noncontrolling interests; the loss attributable to Centene shareholders was $71M ($0.14 a share).
